children: and other U.S. energy shares moved higher as crude prices climbed following renewed military tensions between the United States and Iran around the Strait of Hormuz.
Chevron shares gained 2%, while Exxon Mobil
Oil prices moved above $90 a barrel, with Brent crude rising more than 2% after U.S. forces struck Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island.
Iran responded with attacks on U.S. positions, increasing concerns that further conflict could interfere with shipments through the key oil route.
Higher crude prices could support energy producers' revenue and earnings expectations, although further developments in the region remain an important risk for the sector.

title: Chevron Leads Energy Stocks Rally as U.S.-Iran Conflict Sends Oil Prices Higher
